edges.reason: The tiled-region interpretation explains what length times width counts. The Geometric Measurement Progression develops that interpretation before treating multiplication as a formula; knowing the formula alone does not certify the tiling procedure.
edges.scope: Understanding rectangle and square area formulas as counts of square units

edges.reason: The rectangle/square area formulas count equal square units, so the meaning of area and its uniform unit are part of the asserted result.
edges.scope: interpreting length times width as unit-square count

edges.reason: The earlier concrete money/length treatment gives useful tenths experience. The later node itself introduces tenths and hundredths as decimal fractions, so the link is spiral preparation rather than a distinct necessary concept; Gemini equates reintroducing that content with mandatory prior instruction.
edges.scope: extending decimal meaning from tenths to hundredths

edges.reason: Power-of-ten scaling explains why factor place counts add. The actual criteria compute and locate the point, and can use an area/place-unit model or an established digit-count rule without the separate scaling workflow; retain explanatory preparation.

Multiplication by an integer gives experience placing decimal points. The stated decimal-by-decimal criterion can use the integer-digit product and the sum of factor place counts directly; it does not execute a previously learned decimal-by-integer algorithm.
The unit-price application explicitly uses the total-price equals unit-price times quantity relation. Only that relation is required from the wider quantity-relations endpoint.
Area contexts with two decimal dimensions contain decimal-by-decimal products. The scope is those cases, not integer-quantity repeated-addition examples alone.
edges.scope: area problems with two decimal factors
